title: A General Method for Extending Isoscattering Non-Isospectral Quantum Graphs
authors: Omer Farooq, Michal Lawniczak, Leszek Sirko
abstract: The present paper sets out a general method for extending the isoscattering, non-isospectral quantum graphs. The methodology is illustrated by considering two graphs, denoted by $Γ_1$ and $Γ_2$, which have the same total metric length but different topologies. It is demonstrated that, despite the fact that their scattering matrices are identical, their eigenvalues, denoted by $k_n$, and Euler characteristics differ from one another. The next step in the process is to extend both graphs by affixing the same star graph to each of them. Utilising the Titchmarsh-Weyl M-function formalism, it is proven that the newly constructed, extended graphs are also isoscattering and non-isospectral.
summary: This paper presents a general method to extend quantum graphs that are isoscattering (identical scattering matrices) but non-isospectral (different energy spectra). By analyzing two initial graphs, the authors demonstrate this property and then prove that attaching a standard star graph preserves this intriguing relationship in the extended system.
main_problem: To develop a general mathematical method for extending quantum graphs that exhibit the property of being isoscattering but non-isospectral.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated that the initial pair of graphs ($\Gamma_1, \Gamma_2$) are isoscattering but non-isospectral, and this property is preserved when extending both graphs by affixing an identical star graph ($\Gamma_S$).
method: The analysis relies on the Titchmarsh-Weyl M-function formalism for graph gluing and comparing spectral properties (eigenvalues, Euler characteristic) against scattering matrix calculations.
model_or_system: The system under study is quantum graphs, which are metric graphs governed by a self-adjoint Laplace operator. The model involves comparing two graphs ($\Gamma_1, \Gamma_2$) with the same length but different topologies, and then extending them by attaching a star graph ($\Gamma_S$) at a contact vertex.
key_observables: Scattering matrix ($S(k)$), eigenvalues ($k_n$), multiplicities ($m_n$), and the Euler characteristic ($\chi(\Gamma)$).
important_parameters: Total metric length ($L$), coupling constants, and the structure of the attached star graph ($\Gamma_S$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the validity of the Titchmarsh-Weyl M-function formalism for characterizing scattering properties upon graph extension.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the topologies of the initial graphs ($\Gamma_1$ and $\Gamma_2$). Figure 2 confirms the equality of the scattering matrices ($S_{\Gamma_1}(k) = S_{\Gamma_2}(k)$). Figure 3 shows the construction of the extended graphs ($\Gamma_{1S}$ and $\Gamma_{2S}$).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the initial non-isospectral, isoscattering pair ($\Gamma_1, \Gamma_2$) using spectral and scattering analysis. It then introduces the extension procedure by attaching a star graph ($\Gamma_S$) and proves, using the M-function formalism, that the resulting extended graphs ($\Gamma_{1S}, \Gamma_{2S}$) retain both the isoscattering and non-isospectral characteristics.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to the study of open quantum systems and wave propagation on complex structures, providing a rigorous mathematical framework for understanding how local changes (like adding a star graph) affect global spectral and scattering properties.
